text: Customer inactivity analysis: Days since last order measures the time elapsed since the customer's most recent purchase. A longer inactivity period may indicate reduced purchasing engagement. Interpret it together with total orders and customer history. It is a risk indicator, not confirmed churn.

Order frequency analysis: Total orders provide a measure of the customer's purchase frequency. A low order count may indicate limited repeat purchasing. Interpret it with inactivity and other available customer indicators. Do not assume dissatisfaction from order count alone.

Order cancellation analysis: Cancelled orders can indicate a potential customer or fulfilment concern. Evaluate cancelled orders in relation to total orders. The aggregate cancellation count does not explain why an order was cancelled. Do not invent a cancellation reason.

Delivered order analysis: Delivered order count provides context about completed purchases. Compare delivered orders with total orders and cancelled orders. Aggregate counts cannot identify individual delivery events or specific delivery problems.

Average order value analysis: Average order value describes the average monetary value of customer orders. Interpret it alongside total orders and purchase activity. It does not independently prove customer satisfaction, dissatisfaction or churn.

Evidence limitations: The Olist customer feature profile used by this project contains total orders, delivered orders, cancelled orders, last order date, average order value, days since last order and a retention risk proxy. It does not provide individual delivery delays, review comments or complaint reasons. Investigation must remain within the available evidence.

Retention risk interpretation: An inactivity-based retention risk proxy is not an observed churn label or a confirmed prediction. Describe it as an inactivity signal. Avoid presenting correlation or an indicator as a proven cause of customer behaviour.
